channel.title: FT – Fiction
channel.description: Fiction reviews and articles from the Financial Times.

item.title: Body shocks, lust and Shakespeare’s sonnets — five of the best debut novels
item.description: A teenage girl can’t stop growing in 1850s London, while the Bard’s Dark Lady and Young Man come to life in a modern-day house share

item.title: The best science fiction and graphic novels to read this year
item.description: James Lovegrove and Lucy Scholes select their must-read titles

item.title: The best fiction and fiction in translation to read this year
item.description: Maria Crawford and Ángel Gurría-Quintana select their must-read titles

item.title: The best books for young people to read this year
item.description: James Lovegrove and Suzi Feay select their must-read titles

item.title: The best food, drink and travel books to read this year
item.description: Sophy Roberts and Niki Blasina select their must-read titles

item.title: The best audio books to listen to this year
item.description: Magdalena Miecznicka and Alex Clark select their must-listen titles

item.description: Carl Wilkinson and Suzi Feay select their must-read titles

item.description: Barry Forshaw and Adam LeBor select their must-read titles

item.title: Amazons — Don DeLillo’s puckish ice hockey fable
item.description: The American novelist’s unlikely sex comedy, written under a pseudonym in 1980, has been reissued after the success of steamy TV hit ‘Heated Rivalry’

item.title: The best books of the week
item.description: From Ukraine’s wartime ordeal to 8,000 years of wine and the new novel from Karl Ove Knausgaard. Plus: a fictionalised life of Sergei Eisenstein, a biography of Saki and the collected stories of Ingeborg Bachmann

item.title: The biting short stories and stormy love letters of Ingeborg Bachmann
item.description: Two new collections showcase the work of the Austrian author, along with her turbulent postwar correspondence with Swiss writer Max Frisch

item.title: Arendal — a super-strength shot of Karl Ove Knausgaard
item.description: A car breakdown on a frozen road brings a mid-life marital crisis to the fore in the riveting fifth novel of the ‘Morning Star’ series

item.title: Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy star in heady southern gothic thriller The Good Daughter
item.description: Tragedy strikes again and again in this plot-heavy but impeccably acted family drama on Peacock/Sky

item.title: Eisen by Guzel Yakhina — the man behind the montage
item.description: A fictionalised biography of Sergei Eisenstein turns the Soviet film-maker’s life into a study of art, censorship and psychological torment

item.title: Booker Prize winner says financial crash inspired his novel about alien invasion
item.description: M John Harrison is the oldest person, and the first science fiction writer, to win the prestigious literary prize

item.title: M John Harrison’s ‘The End of Everything’ wins the 2026 Booker Prize for fiction
item.description: The 81-year-old science fiction author who has won acclaim as a genre-busting prose stylist is the oldest winner of the award, for a post-apocalyptic novel that ‘leaves you with a twinge of optimism’

item.title: Cormac McCarthy: A Legacy Revisited — the making of a myth
item.description: Tracy Daugherty’s biography dismantles the legend of the solitary, blood-soaked gunslinger and finds a writer shaped by privilege, patronage and literary connections

item.title: Lessons in Harmony by Jonathan Coe — notes between nations
item.description: A witty historical novel turns the real-life relationship between Ralph Vaughan Williams and Maurice Ravel into a meditation on art, nationhood and love

item.title: Peck & Peck by Bonnie Garmus — poetry and posturing in ’80s New York
item.description: The author follows up ‘Lessons in Chemistry’ with an absurdist coming-of-age tale of publishing, Trumpian editors and trampled dreams

item.title: The Rhyl Poster — inside a traitor’s mind
item.description: Tom McCarthy’s slow-burn, hallucinatory thriller is a plausible portrait of the traumatised psyche of a legal expert turned spy

item.title: Alphaville.We read Liz Truss’s book so you don’t have to
item.description: Alternative histories aren’t always written by the victors

item.title: Virtue and Rosalind — Anne Serre’s reflections in a hall of mirrors
item.description: An innovative, multi-faceted novel suffused with mystery and strange beauty

item.title: Vaim Hotel — Jon Fosse checks back into his world of dislocation and strangeness
item.description: The second part of the Nobel winner’s trilogy follows an unintentional guest in a fictional Norwegian town full of perplexity and uncertainty

item.title: Music Against the Night by Yiyun Li — life in a minor key
item.description: Two largely forgotten pianists of the early 19th century — John Field and Adelaide Percheron — are brought vividly to life in a novel of ambition, memory and music

item.title: The Man with Many Names by Georgi Gospodinov — the ghosts of Bulgaria
item.description: From communist absurdities to villages emptied by emigration, this collection of stories finds wit and tenderness in the country’s turbulent past
